llm_findings: One causal intervention: --ngram-rms-fp32 alone changes the n-gram RMSProp precision policy, without enabling the NKI kernel or changing model shape, schedule, or table/gradient dtype. Authoritative train.py lines 741–751 and 5933–5948 support this independent option. Its precise scope includes FP32 second-moment storage AND FP32 denominator/update arithmetic, not merely intermediate state math.
Both pinned control ledger rows confirm active BF16 n-gram tables with RMSProp, rms_fp32_state_math=False, and nki_rms=False, establishing an applicable baseline.

The cited fs-w3/fs-w4 ledger results support the reported -0.000621 BPB and +16 steps. The proposal correctly treats this as suggestive rather than isolating evidence because the historical candidate also enabled NKI and changed commits.
No closed FP32-only n-gram RMSProp direction is identified in the supplied decision log or parked-direction list. The historical fused-kernel experiment is causally distinct from this ablation.

This optimizer precision change is permitted by README.md and introduces no pretrained weights, external data, or evaluator changes. The declared BPB and step-count thresholds make the expected benefit falsifiable against the controller-managed seed-42 full-chip matched control.

The claimed rounding-bias removal and gathered-row-only cost remain hypotheses, not established repository facts. index_gather=True alone does not prove sparse optimizer execution; assess the experiment by measured final BPB and throughput rather than assuming that mechanism.
